metadata.name: Global Financial Crisis 2008
metadata.description: Lehman Brothers collapse and ensuing global credit crisis. Severe flight-to-quality in rates, massive credit spread widening, equity crash, and volatility spike. Market-data identifiers in this template (e.g. USD-SOFR, USD-IG, SPX_VOL) are modern placeholders, not historical instruments; to match your market data, build the template (or one of its components) and edit the market-data identifiers in the resulting spec's operations before applying it.

metadata.name: COVID 2020 Market Shock
metadata.description: Pandemic-driven market dislocation in March 2020. Emergency rate cuts, sharp credit widening, an equity crash, volatility spike, and broad USD strength. Market-data identifiers in this template (e.g. USD-SOFR, USD-IG, SPX_VOL) are modern placeholders, not historical instruments; to match your market data, build the template (or one of its components) and edit the market-data identifiers in the resulting spec's operations before applying it.

metadata.name: 2022 Fed Hiking Cycle
metadata.description: Inflation-driven 2022 hiking cycle. Sharp rate repricing, wider credit spreads, equity drawdowns, higher volatility, and a stronger USD. Market-data identifiers in this template (e.g. USD-SOFR, USD-IG, SPX_VOL) are modern placeholders, not historical instruments; to match your market data, build the template (or one of its components) and edit the market-data identifiers in the resulting spec's operations before applying it.

metadata.name: SVB / Regional Banking Crisis 2023
metadata.description: March 2023 regional banking stress after Silicon Valley Bank failed. Front-end rates rallied, regional bank spreads widened, equities sold off, volatility rose, and the USD strengthened modestly. Market-data identifiers in this template (e.g. USD-SOFR, USD-IG, SPX_VOL) are modern placeholders, not historical instruments; to match your market data, build the template (or one of its components) and edit the market-data identifiers in the resulting spec's operations before applying it. The credit component is an instrument-level spread shock and requires a portfolio of instruments in the execution context to take effect.
